title: Structured-literacy teaching requirements: primary-source ledger
purpose: Durable requirements requested by the user before saved lesson preparation; no implementation or clinical-outcome claim.
accessPolicy: Only substantive primary/official resources listed as read. Scope limitations are per source; search snippets and navigation-only pages are not evidence.

sources.title: Structured Literacy: Effective Instruction for Students with Dyslexia and Related Reading Difficulties
sources.keyFinding: Explicit, planned, cumulative language instruction combines teacher modeling, practice, feedback and responsive pacing. Content reaches beyond phonemes into spelling, word structure and comprehension.
sources.application: Keep tutor control and cumulative review; do not equate a card/game collection with a complete intervention.
sources.limitations: Article text read; not the linked downloadable manual. Its instructional term diagnostic does not authorize software diagnosis.

sources.title: Dyslexia in Children
sources.keyFinding: Take Flight addresses phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary and comprehension and is taught by trained Academic Language Therapists.
sources.application: Support a tutor working within their program without claiming official affiliation or reproducing an unseen curriculum.
sources.limitations: Public page read, including program description. Original care/dyslexia URL redirected here; proprietary program materials were not accessed.

sources.title: Research at a Glance: Take Flight
sources.keyFinding: The program summary describes a two-year intervention with specialized therapist training and follow-up of graduating groups.
sources.application: Keep the distinction between a trained intervention program and our original teaching workspace.
sources.limitations: One-page PDF text read. Not an independent replication, full study appraisal or evidence for this app.

sources.title: Glossary
sources.keyFinding: Elkonin boxes represent individual sounds; letters or letter combinations can later map those sounds. Blendable consonant models avoid an added schwa.
sources.application: Keep tutor-selected phoneme counts, digraph units and accurate consonant audio.
sources.limitations: Relevant glossary definitions read; some phonics labels simplify phonetic analysis and should not be treated as universal IPA.

sources.title: UFLI Sound Wall Materials
sources.keyFinding: This sound-wall set pairs articulatory mouth cues with sound cards and adds taught grapheme correspondences; its organization is program specific.
sources.application: Use as an inventory comparison rather than importing a second deck or equating sound count with photograph count.
sources.limitations: PDF text read, including introduction, labels and grapheme pages. Not a visual/phonetic validation of every photograph or access to the UFLI manual.

sources.title: How to Pronounce the English Phonemes: An Interactive Demo
sources.keyFinding: The resource connects pronunciation, articulatory features, spellings and examples for consonants and vowels.
sources.application: Review teaching cues as a coordinated set; a plausible face photograph alone is insufficient.
sources.limitations: Surrounding article read. Embedded two-page interactive was not fully operated and its audio was not audited.

sources.title: How to Teach Articulation: Consonant Pairs
sources.keyFinding: Related consonants can share placement while differing in voicing; familiar group names are teaching cues rather than interchangeable sounds.
sources.application: Allow shared appropriate photographs while keeping sound identity and airflow/voicing instructions distinct.
sources.limitations: Substantive prose/table read. The page credits licensed Kid Lips images; those are not app assets or evidence of Take Flight nomenclature.

sources.title: How to Teach Articulation: Vowels, Diphthongs, and Vowel-r
sources.keyFinding: Vowel instruction distinguishes changing mouth gestures, stress and vowel-r patterns; a vowel-valley display is optional rather than necessary for every learner.
sources.application: Keep movement/stress cues and tutor choice; do not force a dense full sound wall onto the student.
sources.limitations: Vowel prose and printed transcript read; videos not watched or listened to. Counts and labels reflect this resource, not a universal analysis.

sources.title: Articulation and Students who Speak African American English
sources.keyFinding: Dialect differences are rule-governed language variation, not automatically articulation errors or deficits.
sources.application: Identify the model accent and avoid automatic penalties or deficit labels for home pronunciation.
sources.limitations: Main guidance and available transcript read; no live classroom observation or app speech-scoring validation.

sources.title: Foundational Skills to Support Reading for Understanding in Kindergarten Through 3rd Grade
sources.publisher: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
sources.keyFinding: The guide recommends language instruction, sound-letter linking, decoding/word writing and daily connected-text reading, with different evidence ratings.
sources.application: Keep literacy goals broader than games and mouth cards and avoid transferring its evidence ratings to our app.
sources.limitations: Recommendations and scope read. The landing page labels July 2016 release and December 2019 revision.

sources.title: Foundational Skills to Support Reading for Understanding in Kindergarten Through 3rd Grade (full guide)
sources.publisher: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
sources.keyFinding: The examples match boxes to phonemes, use counters/tiles according to print knowledge, distinguish blends from digraphs, and address unwanted schwa during blending.
sources.application: Test sound counts and preserve tutor-guided oral-to-print mapping and accurate consonant models.
sources.limitations: Relevant printed pages 17–20 and 31 plus introduction read, not all 123 PDF pages or every underlying study. PDF page numbering differs from printed numbering.

sources.title: The Consonants of American English
sources.publisher: University of California, Irvine OpenCourseWare; Marla Yoshida
sources.keyFinding: Consonants differ by voicing, place and manner; nasal airflow differs from stops, and /wh/ contrasts vary among speakers.
sources.application: Review each grouped label without erasing sound distinctions or enforcing optional accent contrasts.
sources.limitations: Relevant PDF pages 1–5 read, not every exercise. Pronunciation teaching guidance, not a dyslexia intervention trial.

sources.title: The Vowels of American English
sources.publisher: University of California, Irvine OpenCourseWare; Marla Yoshida
sources.keyFinding: Vowels vary across accents and speakers; letters are not vowel sounds, and lip posture alone is an imperfect indicator.
sources.application: Label accent-sensitive targets, distinguish print from sounds, and avoid requiring one exaggerated face shape.
sources.limitations: Relevant PDF pages 1–5 read, not all 15 pages. Its vowel inventory is an analysis choice, not a required photo count.

localEvidence.finding: 16 grouped families with original phonics labels; shared front-photo keys do not identify identical airflow or vowel targets.
47 developer reference entries: 40 core targets, 6 sequences, 1 dialect target; General American scope and no official Take Flight affiliation.
Default plan exports 12 additions into Mouth Pictures at orders 17–28; all-sounds is an explicit developer-reference alternative.
Existing checks map family labels to reference IDs and assert 16+12=28 coverage without expanding the grouped library to 47. Tests inspected, not executed for this documentation task.
Shared 1200x1200 card frame with one face photograph, title, instruction, anatomical diagram and sound text.
Uses the same frame for additions; movement is described in text/diagram without a second photograph.
Checks the full 28-card frame, nonempty photograph/diagram, shared geometry, banner and text regions. Not a clinical accuracy test.
Checks one mouth region, fitting text, sequence wording and unstressed schwa example.
Eight generated posture assets have prompts, reference filename, intended-use limitations and SHA-256 provenance; appearance is not phonetic validation.
Renders the 16 families into JPEG/CSV for the existing library import.
Default 12-addition export validates missing content and duplicate rendered hashes and retains card/region metadata.
Stable identities and image hashes are preflighted; metadata uses Cosmos Mongo pictures collection, bytes use private Blob library container. No cloud inventory was read.
Teacher-selected count, bounded taps and exercise epoch; count is not inferred from letters.

inventorySnapshot.basis: Local ES module imports and source inspection, not live database/Blob queries
inventorySnapshot.duplicateCaution: Stable card IDs and rendered hashes differ from shared source photographs; semantic target review is also necessary.

userRequirements: Consistent existing aqua/white card style: one face photograph, title, instruction, one anatomy diagram, sound/example text.
No title/example separator such as Long I — pie; preserve phonics diacritics.
No duplicate complete cards or second production import of the 47-entry developer reference.
Retain direct Add face, full-card view, Magic Select including meaningful non-face regions, and manual selection.
Preserve search/scroll, manageable clear-space placement, overlap/layer information and student face-size restriction.
Tutor controls sequence and revealing materials; saved manual Review/Build words/Dictation/Read and private Review next time notes follow board pages.
Private answers, word lists and notes never go onto the student wire merely hidden in the UI.
Custom original tools can support Take Flight tutors without claiming official certification or endorsement.

handwrittenNote.provenance: User-provided photograph in conversation; original temporary image file no longer available locally. Legible phrases preserved in companion Markdown.
handwrittenNote.certaintyPolicy: Do not infer exact vowel symbols, first tongue label final word, cramped h annotation, or isolated scraper association. Reconfirm before naming or generating cards.

limits: This is guidance for product implementation, not a complete curriculum, diagnostic instrument, or proof of intervention efficacy.
No saved-lesson code, cloud changes, live imports, or runtime service changes were made.
No claim of full audio review, current live Blob counts or a therapist review of every existing card.
